items.description: The isSentimentLevel type predicate does `(SENTIMENT_FILTER_IDS as readonly string[]).includes(value)`, an `as` type cast that violates the project's 'no type casts' style rule. Reviewer recommended a `Set<string>` lookup instead, which avoids the cast entirely.

Four `item!.sentiment` non-null assertions (lines 142, 161, 177, 191) violate the project's 'no non-null assertions' style rule. The preceding `expect(item).toBeDefined()` is only a runtime check and does not narrow the TypeScript type, so the `!` silently suppresses the compile-time null check.

The security-guard test 'should silently drop the sentiments filter for client callers' asserts `total === 3` and that two other beneficiaries are present, but never asserts the critical-sentiment beneficiary is also included. A future regression that returned all 3 beneficiaries while specifically excluding the critical one would still pass this test — a real gap in a test meant to guard client-side sentiment-filter authorization.

`CrSentimentLevel` is imported directly from `@/case-radar/analysis/analysis.module` in this DTO (and in responses.dto.ts and beneficiary-query.service.ts), bypassing the beneficiary-views/BeneficiaryViewService cross-module chokepoint this PR otherwise establishes for case-radar access, leaving two independent case-radar coupling points instead of one.

The sentiment-cell loading skeleton used `rounded-full` (pill shape), but the actual rendered SentimentBadge uses `rounded` (link variant) or no rounding (plain span variant), producing a visible shape pop when the real data loads in.

`applySentimentFilterGuard` strips the `sentiments` field only on the `!enabled` branch (destructuring it out); the staff+enabled branch returns `{ ...query, userIds }` and leaves `sentiments` on the object. `buildWhere` ignores the field today so there is no active bug, but the asymmetry is confusing and a latent risk if `buildWhere` ever starts reading it.

`validatedSentiments = sentiments.filter(isSentimentLevel)` is recomputed on every render, producing a new array reference that feeds into the TanStack Query queryKey. TanStack deep-equals queryKeys so this doesn't cause spurious refetches today, but it is an unnecessary per-render allocation and a risk if any future consumer assumes referential stability.

The `'use client'` directive sits on this re-export shim rather than on the canonical `apps/web/src/shared/components/sentiment-badge.tsx`, which actually uses `Link` and `MouseEventHandler` and needs the directive. Consumers that import the canonical path directly (bypassing the shim) would not get the directive at all.
